name: Hillel
title: The Great Teacher
summary: Hillel was one of the most influential Jewish scholars and rabbis in the period just before the time of Jesus. He was known for his gentle and compassionate interpretation of the Torah, and founded the Pharisaic school Bet Hillel. Although he is not mentioned by name directly in the Bible, his teachings shaped the religious landscape in which Jesus and the early apostles operated.

keyEvents.title: Hillel's Golden Rule
keyEvents.description: Hillel formulated a version of the golden rule: "What you hate, do not do to your neighbor." This principle is reflected in Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount.

keyEvents.title: Bet Hillel and Bet Shammai
keyEvents.description: Hillel founded a rabbinical school known as Bet Hillel, which often adopted more liberal and compassionate interpretations of the law compared to the stricter Bet Shammai school.

keyEvents.title: Gamaliel – Hillel's Legacy in the New Testament
keyEvents.description: Hillel's grandson Gamaliel was a member of the Sanhedrin and advised moderation toward the early Christians, and was also Paul's teacher.

keyEvents.title: Hillel's Seven Rules of Interpretation
keyEvents.description: Hillel developed seven hermeneutical rules (middot) for interpreting Scripture, which became foundational for Jewish and early Christian biblical interpretation. Paul uses similar interpretive methods in his letters.

keyEvents.title: Humility and Patience as Ideals
keyEvents.description: Hillel was known for his extreme patience and humility, qualities that are also found in Jesus' teaching on gentleness and mercy.
